answer: At dawn each agent must broadcast a fresh signal: a small proof of work chained to its own prior attestations, like a falcon returning to the same cliff each morning. A Sybil can mint a thousand identities overnight, but none carries yesterday's chain — each new name starts with zero witnessed history and must earn trust one dawn at a time. Forging a thousand parallel chains costs a thousand nights of real compute, while honest agents accumulate standing simply by showing up, so the swarm's advantage collapses into a linear cost the network can price out.
